title: Evaluation of the geologic and hydrologic factors related to the waste-storage potential of Mesozoic aquifers in the southern part of the Atlantic coastal plain, South Carolina and Georgia
citation: Brown, P.M., Brown, D.L., Reid, M.S., and Lloyd, O.B., 1979, Evaluation of the geologic and hydrologic factors related to the waste-storage potential of Mesozoic aquifers in the southern part of the Atlantic coastal plain, South Carolina and Georgia: U.S. Geological Survey Professional Paper 1088, map scale 1:2,000,000.
notes:
USGS PP 1088 (Brown and others, 1979), packet 1: plates 1-11 (OCR) and front matter (pages 12-17). Plate 1 stratigraphic cross sections A-A' to H-H' and the plate map faces are OCR noise and are not digitized; recorded here are the map types: structure on pre-Unit H(?) basement and unit thickness maps (plate 2), and structural-top and thickness maps of Units F to A (plates 5-10). Units G(?) and H(?) maps (plates 3-4) are left out because the text states these units are absent in South Carolina; plate 11 isochlor maps not itemized. Contour values not read. SUBSURFACE: sections and contour values not digitized.
PP 1088 packet 2 (pages 18-36): informal chronostratigraphic Units A-H(?) and basement. Units G(?) and H(?) are absent in South Carolina according to the text and are not recorded. Georgia-specific values (Savannah basin, Apalachicola embayment, Central Georgia uplift, waste-storage areas in table 2, Georgia isochlors) left out. Sand-shale geometry text not itemized. SUBSURFACE: none beyond the key-well tables in packet 3.
PP 1088 packet 3 (pages 38-53): key-well network tables (table 6) for the South Carolina wells only (Aiken, Barnwell, Charleston, Dorchester, Georgetown, Horry Counties); Georgia and North Carolina wells left out. Unit tops are printed as depth below mean sea level (+ = above) and stored as such; unit thicknesses, remarks (top of Triassic(?) or crystalline rock) and the garbled SC-GEO-T-30 row are not recorded; 'abs.' (absent) and dashes are not values. Tables 7-8 (wells with waste-storage potential, chloride data) concern Georgia and are not itemized. SUBSURFACE: unit tops at key wells.
